item: Incidence criterion (CT thm:criterion): a finite ℓ+1-regular incidence system of girth ≥ 12 plus vectors x_v with Σ_V x_v x_v^T = -I_m, Σ_{v∈f} x_v x_v^T = 0 and m < t ≤ mℓ^2 over a char-2 field yields a finitely presented G and a, b ∈ K[G] with ab = 1, ba ≠ 1
item_type: F5 (change of representation; F3 flavour) — a lemma-type certificate
lean_status_why: ChosenCriterion.products (ChosenCriterion.lean:42) proves the criterion's conclusion from its hypotheses by the paper's own route (subgroup averages, rectangular identity, HNN character twist, packing, finite block), and it is on the comparator path of KaplanskyDirectFiniteness and KaplanskyFinitelyPresented; the statement is split and Skolemized, and finite presentation is proved only for the prescribed instance.
lean_gaps: No single Lean declaration states thm:criterion. It is split into a characteristic-free algebraic core, CharacterTwist.matrix_products (CharacterFormulas.lean:25), and a char-2 instantiation, ChosenCriterion.products (ChosenCriterion.lean:42).

'Every v lies in exactly ℓ+1 members of F' is replaced by an explicit bijection assign : {f // v ∈ Inc f} ≃ Option (ZMod ℓ), matching faces to the ℓ+1 lines of F_ℓ^2. These are equivalent up to a choice.
't ≤ mκ' is replaced by a supplied slot map slot : V → m and forms α : V → (F_ℓ^2 →* Z/ℓ) with distinct (slot, α) pairs (hα). These are equivalent, since there are κ forms.

The conclusion for general data gives only a finitely generated group (instance groupFG). Finite presentation and an element of order ℓ are proved only for the prescribed data (PrescribedPresentation.prescribed_finitelyPresented, OddTorsion.prescribed_odd_prime_order).

CharacterTwist.square_witnesses (AlgebraicCriterion.lean:63), the target the novelty analysis proposed for P-C1, is NOT on the comparator proof path according to the text-level extractor. The live route is matrix_products → PackingFormulas.prescribed_packing_products, so use ChosenCriterion.products or matrix_products as the discoverability target.

The comparators are weaker than the family headline. TF (torsion-free, over F_2) is not formalized. CT's comparators keep torsion and do not assert K = F_2. Nonsoficity and the CT cellular-automaton statement are not formalized.

variable {K V F m : Type} [Field K] [CharP K 2]
variable [Fintype V] [Fintype F] [Fintype m]
variable (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime]

local instance modulusNeZero : NeZero ℓ := inferInstance

variable (Inc : F → Finset V)
variable (assign : ∀ v, {f : F // v ∈ Inc f} ≃ Option (ZMod ℓ))

variable (v₀ : V) (α : V → GluedGroup.PointGroup ℓ →* Multiplicative (ZMod ℓ))

abbrev inclusion := point Inc ℓ assign
abbrev inclusion_injective := point_injective Inc ℓ assign hInc hg
abbrev Extension := CharacterTwist.L (inclusion ℓ Inc assign)
  (inclusion_injective ℓ Inc assign hInc hg) v₀ α
abbrev Group := Extension ℓ Inc assign hInc hg v₀ α ×
  FiniteBlock.Auxiliary m (Multiplicative (ZMod ℓ))

lean_source.kind: theorem (characteristic-free algebraic core; on the comparator path)
lean_source.text:
theorem matrix_products {F : Type u_7} [Fintype F]
    (X : Matrix m V K) (Inc : F → Finset V)
    (lineSum : F → MonoidAlgebra K (L ι hi v₀ α))
    (hdec : ∀ v, P (K := K) ι hi v₀ α v =
      1 + ∑ f : {f : F // v ∈ Inc f}, (lineSum f.val - 1))
    (hglobal : X * X.transpose = 1)
    (hlocal : ∀ f i j, ∑ v ∈ Inc f, X i v * X j v = 0)
    (hlt : Fintype.card m < Fintype.card V)
    (hA : (Fintype.card A : K) ≠ 0) (hC : (Fintype.card C : K) ≠ 0)
    (slot : V → m) (hξ : Function.Injective ξ)
    (hα : ∀ v w, v ≠ w → slot v = slot w → α v ≠ α w) :
    aMatrix ι hi v₀ α ξ X slot * bMatrix ι hi v₀ α ξ X slot=1 ∧
    bMatrix ι hi v₀ α ξ X slot * aMatrix ι hi v₀ α ξ X slot≠1 := by

lean_source.kind: theorem (existential twin of matrix_products; NOT on the comparator proof path per extractor)

theorem square_witnesses {F : Type u_9} [Fintype F]
    (X : Matrix m V K) (Inc : F → Finset V)
    (lineSum : F → MonoidAlgebra K (L ι hi v₀ α))
    (hdec : ∀ v, P (K := K) ι hi v₀ α v =
      1 + ∑ f : {f : F // v ∈ Inc f}, (lineSum f.val - 1))
    (hglobal : X * X.transpose = 1)
    (hlocal : ∀ f i j, ∑ v ∈ Inc f, X i v * X j v = 0)
    (hlt : Fintype.card m < Fintype.card V)
    (hA : (Fintype.card A : K) ≠ 0) (hC : (Fintype.card C : K) ≠ 0)
    (slot : V → m) (hξ : Function.Injective ξ)
    (hα : ∀ v w, v ≠ w → slot v = slot w → α v ≠ α w) :
    ∃ a b : Matrix m m (MonoidAlgebra K (L ι hi v₀ α)), a * b = 1 ∧ b * a ≠ 1 := by

lean_source.name: OAI.KaplanskyCounterexample.Rectangular.U / T / identities
lean_source.kind: def + theorem (glued subgroup averages give UP = U, PT = T, UT = 1)
lean_source.text:
def U (X : Matrix m V K) (P : V → R) : Matrix m V R := fun i v => X i v • P v
def T (X : Matrix m V K) (P : V → R) : Matrix V m R := fun v i => X i v • P v

omit [Fintype m] in
theorem identities (X : Matrix m V K) (P : V → R) (L : F → R)
    (Inc : F → Finset V)
    (hP : ∀ v, P v * P v = P v)
    (hdec : ∀ v, P v = 1 + ∑ f : {f : F // v ∈ Inc f}, (L f - 1))
    (hglobal : X * X.transpose = 1)
    (hlocal : ∀ f i j, ∑ v ∈ Inc f, X i v * X j v = 0) :
    U X P * Matrix.diagonal P = U X P ∧
      Matrix.diagonal P * T X P = T X P ∧ U X P * T X P = 1 := by

lemma subgroup_decomposition {K : Type u_3} [CommRing K] (v : V) :

open_problems.title: O1. Kaplansky direct finiteness in every odd characteristic p (e.g. p = 3)
open_problems.statement: For a given odd prime p, is there a finite field K of characteristic p and a group G with K[G] not directly finite?
open_problems.reference: Kaplansky 1972 (Fields and Rings, pp. 122–123); Elek–Szabó arXiv:math/0305440; the release settles p = 2 (CT) and one specific huge prime (OD) only
open_problems.status: open for every odd prime other than OD's p (as of 2026-10-09; web check found no other odd-characteristic result)
open_problems.obstruction_match: exact: the only use of characteristic 2 in CT is that the regular degree D = ℓ+1 must vanish in K (summing the line identities gives D·Σ_V W_v = 0 while Σ_V W_v = -I) — CT 03-pairing.tex:103-106 and 05-prescription.tex:64. In characteristic p this is supplied by choosing ℓ ≡ -1 mod q^100 with q = p^h (CT already picks ℓ ≡ -1 mod q^100 with q = 2^h), which also gives κ = ℓ^2 ≡ 1 in K.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Keep thm:criterion and §§2–3 verbatim (Lean core CharacterTwist.matrix_products is characteristic-free: it needs only |A|, |C| ≠ 0 in K and the abstract decomposition hypothesis). Pairing: use d0 = ⌊(q-2)/2⌋ (Lean Pairing uses Nat division and is stated 'with no characteristic simplification'). Hypergraph: rerun the LLL/slab construction with q = p^h; it uses q | D and q-element lines, not parity (paper §4 text); Lean's CharP Q 2 assumptions appear in PlaneOperators/FrameTransport/SlabAssembly/PrescribedIncidence and look incidental (used to pick a quadratic extension). Risks: hole-size estimates for odd q; the OD paper's remark that the two methods 'retain distinct coefficient hypotheses' suggests the producer did not believe or did not try this extension.
open_problems.payoff: high (with Kaplansky's char-0 theorem, would settle DF in every characteristic; best possible device-reuse evidence: same certificate, new conjecture instance)

open_problems.title: O5. Test candidate groups for embedded criterion configurations (Thompson's V, Ã2-lattices, Kac–Moody lattices)
open_problems.statement: Does a given group of unknown soficity (e.g. Thompson's group V, cocompact lattices in Ã2-buildings) contain finite subgroups F_ℓ^2 glued along lines over a girth ≥ 12 incidence system carrying a pairing with t < mℓ^2? Such a configuration would make the group nonsofic.
open_problems.reference: Pestov arXiv:0804.3968 (soficity of specific groups open); OpenAI's August nonsofic result used the unit group of the Leavitt algebra and Thompson's V (press: https://thenextweb.com/news/openai-astra-model-ten-math-proofs-non-sofic-groups)
open_problems.obstruction_match: the criterion as a nonsoficity test (finite certificate against rank functions)
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Groups with rich elementary-abelian finite subgroup lattices (Ã2 lattices: vertex stabilizers contain (F_q)^2-type subgroups; incidence girth 6 in the building, so girth 12 needs passing to suitable configurations). Low prior: the criterion needs injectivity of the whole colimit into the target group.

lean_feasibility.statable_with: Thompson's V / buildings not in Mathlib

release_reuse.summary: No in-release reuse of the incidence criterion as a device.
release_reuse.OD (odd characteristic, Sep 26): Sibling SCHEMA, not reuse. Same architecture type (local finite-group idempotents glued along a combinatorial structure, a rectangular/low-rank identity, a size ratio beating the rank bound), but a different local mechanism (annihilated high-degree subspace of a modular translation representation; low-rank fit of a triangle-free graph). The OD paper says 'The characteristic-two theorem is not an input to this odd-prime argument' (OD 01-introduction.tex:57-58). Lean: OddKaplansky imports only DirectFiniteness.ReducedWalks.
release_reuse.DT (Determinant Conjecture, Sep 23): Theorem corollary: Lean uses only the existential main_theorem.
release_reuse.TF (torsion-free headline, Oct 4): No reuse: TF cites CT only for context ('a finitely presented group with odd-order torsion', TF introduction.tex:48) and builds on family 196's parity mechanism.
release_reuse.Family 285 (Baum–Connes / Kadison–Kaplan: Checked text of the three manuscripts: voltage covers, LPS expanders, lamplighter spectral methods; no incidence criterion.

family_196_precedent.question: Is the 'reported model-produced precedent from family 196' a precedent for the incidence criterion?
family_196_precedent.finding: No. Family 196's paper (ZD, 'A Torsion-Free Group Algebra with Zero Divisors', dated 2026-09-23, the same day as CT) builds a zero product αβ = 0 from two labelled graphs coned off in a 2-complex: odd-degree product graphs have even components, which cancel in characteristic 2. It contains no subgroup averages, no rectangular identity UT = I_m, no character packing and no rank-violating size inequality. The shortlist's 'against' note refers to the family's HEADLINE manuscript TF (Oct 4), which adapts ZD ('develops the graph and cone construction of [ZD]'); TF is not the source of the criterion and is not formalized.
shared_themes: characteristic 2 used to make an even incidence count vanish (ZD: even component sizes; CT: D = ℓ+1 even)
finite-geometry incidence data (ZD: lines of a projective plane as label types; CT: affine lines and the ℓ+1 lines of F_ℓ^2)
family_196_precedent.verdict: Thematic overlap only; same-day, model-produced; not an earlier equivalent. No downgrade of the criterion from 196.

negative_controls.title: Characteristic 0 (Kaplansky: K[G] is stably finite)
negative_controls.why: Proved-false analogue: the criterion's hypotheses are unsatisfiable when char K ∤ ℓ+1, since summing the line identities gives (ℓ+1)·Σ_V x_v x_v^T = 0 while Σ_V x_v x_v^T = -I. In char 0 this is a contradiction. A prover with the criterion must not 'find' data over ℚ.

negative_controls.title: Sofic groups (Elek–Szabó) and residually amenable groups (Ara–O'Meara–Perera)
negative_controls.why: Direct finiteness is a theorem there; no criterion configuration can embed in a sofic group.

negative_controls.title: Torsion-free groups (TF / Kaplansky zero-divisor setting)
negative_controls.why: The criterion needs finite subgroups for its averaging idempotents; it cannot produce the torsion-free headline. TF needed family 196's different mechanism.

top5.target: O1: DF in odd characteristic p (e.g. p = 3)
top5.argument: The decisive device-reuse test. The criterion's only use of characteristic 2 is to make the degree ℓ+1 vanish, which ℓ ≡ -1 mod p^{100h} supplies in characteristic p; the Lean core (CharacterTwist.matrix_products, Rectangular.identities, Pairing.sum_complement_gram) is already characteristic-free. Statable now. If a prover with the criterion in its library proves the p = 3 statement much faster than without it, that is a downstream speedup on a theorem the release does not contain.

top5.target: Weakened OddKaplansky (∃ odd p) — speedup target
top5.argument: The same experiment measured against an existing formal proof: OD's 13,061-line Lean for a stronger fixed-prime statement. Note that the exact OD comparator (|K| = p^4) is out of reach of the criterion, so compare on the weakened statement.

Same certificate, new witnesses: decidable hypotheses on finite data, so a found instance plus ChosenCriterion.products yields a checked counterexample. Tests whether the design generates other witnesses.

top5.target: O4: normalized Sylvester rank functions in positive characteristic
top5.argument: Under 300 lines to define rank functions; the criterion data refute the existence of a normalized rank function on K[N] in two lines. Corollary-like, so it scores reach rather than a jump.

top5.target: O3: hyperbolic nonsofic group via the glued group N
top5.argument: Highest payoff, lowest confidence, not Lean-usable. Worth an expert check on whether N's development is nonpositively curved.
